LESSON: FUNCTIONAL WRITING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.8: Functional writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Functional writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do you write?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify parts of a sentence for communication
2. appreciate the role of writing skills for communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: FUNCTIONAL WRITING
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Functional writing helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: FUNCTIONAL WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify parts of a sentence for communication

What this means
In this part you learn to identify parts of a sentence for communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify parts of a sentence for communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Functional writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify parts of a sentence for communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the role of writing skills for communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of writing skills for communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of writing skills for communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Functional writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of writing skills for communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Functional writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Functional writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify parts of a sentence for communication)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Functional writing to a partner. (skill: appreciate the role of writing skills for communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Functional writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify parts of a sentence for communication.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of writing skills for communication.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Functional writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Functional writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Functional writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do you write?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Functional writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify parts of a sentence for communication.
5. Be able to: appreciate the role of writing skills for communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
